title: Joe-1
prompt: The Soviet Union has tested an atomic bomb. How should {country} explain a world with two nuclear powers?

effect.text: A second nuclear power changes the balance. American leaders accelerate work on a hydrogen bomb.
effect.insight: An opponent’s breakthrough can become an argument for your next weapon.

effect.text: Secrecy delays public debate, but evidence and leaks make silence harder to sustain.
effect.insight: Protecting confidence today can undermine trust when concealed information emerges.

title: A signal from space
prompt: Sputnik passes above every capital. People in {country} look up and ask who is ahead.

effect.text: The orbiting satellite turns science education and rockets into national priorities.
effect.insight: A technological demonstration can change budgets far beyond the laboratory.

effect.text: Public concern about an apparent missile gap outgrows the official reassurance.
effect.insight: Dismissing a rival’s achievement leaves others to define what it means.

title: The plane that did not come home
prompt: A U-2 spy plane is shot down over the Soviet Union. Choose the public position {country} supports.

effect.text: The summit collapses amid the spy-plane dispute.
effect.insight: Diplomacy depends on trust as well as what each side already knows.

effect.text: Evidence of the flight turns a denial into a public embarrassment.
effect.insight: A cover story fails when the other side holds the evidence.

title: Six days, a changed map
prompt: War in the Middle East draws in the superpower rivalry. What position does {country} take?

effect.text: Military defeat and victory deepen dependence on outside patrons.
effect.insight: Local wars become international crises when allies make them tests of credibility.

effect.text: Resolution 242 becomes a disputed framework for negotiations.
effect.insight: A shared diplomatic text can create a channel even when its meaning is contested.

title: Footprints on another world
prompt: People gather around television sets as Apollo 11 reaches the Moon. How does {country} cover it?

effect.text: Mission control watches the landing in the Sea of Tranquility. The audience is worldwide.
effect.insight: A scientific achievement can shape perceptions of an entire political system.

effect.text: Foreign broadcasts and word of mouth carry the news anyway.
effect.insight: Information crosses borders even when official media stay quiet.

title: The price of oil
prompt: Oil prices rise sharply. The costs reach households and factories in {country}.

effect.text: Efficiency and new energy investment ease dependence over time.
effect.insight: Short-term sacrifice can reduce the leverage held by a vital supplier.

effect.text: Subsidies soften the immediate shock while debt and inflation build.
effect.insight: Making a cost less visible does not make it disappear.

title: One man says no
prompt: On 26 September, a Soviet warning system reports five incoming US missiles. Duty officer Stanislav Petrov judges it a false alarm.

effect.text: Petrov reports a false alarm. Satellite reflections, not incoming missiles, triggered the warning.
effect.insight: Judgment by someone outside the cabinet can interrupt a dangerous chain of escalation.

title: An invisible cloud
prompt: Chernobyl has released radioactive material across borders. How should {country} respond to the first reports?

effect.text: Swedish radiation monitoring helps expose a disaster that cannot stay within national borders.
effect.insight: Independent measurements can challenge an official account.

effect.text: Public events proceed while the danger remains concealed. Trust falls when the scale becomes clear.
effect.insight: Withholding health information can trade brief calm for lasting distrust.
